# Write the title

Write a short, familiar noun phrase naming the overall topic defined by the final `meaning`. Choose the name a reader would look for when browsing information about that topic.

Keep directly related activities, products, participants, resources and detailed conditions in `meaning`. Include one of them in the title only when it is needed to distinguish the topic's identity. The title names the topic; it does not restate everything admitted by its definition.

Choose the shortest clear wording that remains a faithful summary. Avoid inventories of the topic's contents and vague abstractions. Keep the established meaning unchanged while choosing the title.

# Synthetic example

The title names the overall blue-panel topic. Its meaning states the component relationship; the title need not list text panels and indicator lights.

# Output
- `title`: a short, familiar name summarizing the topic defined by `meaning`.
